amy: Preflight: change window in ~3h for release v2.4.0. Adding the safety-signal gate runbook link — please ack if you can monitor. https://intra.redwood/runbooks/safety-signal :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started on prod-dedicated-1 (canary id c-1726). Initial traffic 5%. Auto-monitoring hooked.

jordan: Quick Q — what's the explicit rollback trigger? I want the threshold we use for automatic unpin so SRE/Support know when to act.

amy: From the runbook (short):
```
# safety-signal gate excerpt
if request_error_rate_1m > 0.5%:
  trigger emergency-unpin
elif p95_latency_ms > 1200 for 3m:
  begin controlled-backout
# notify: @sre-oncall, @support, #incidents
```

mike: No database schema changes in this release, right? Confirming no long migrations.

amy: Correct — no schema changes, no migrations. :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: I am on-call and will watch dashboards + pager. If error spikes hit the threshold I'll run the escape-hatch steps in the runbook and coordinate the unpin. Add me to the incident timeline.

jordan: Ack. If I need to unpin I'll run the rollback helper: `/ops/unpin.sh c-1726` and post the runbook checklist when I start.

deploy-bot: Canary c-1726: reached 10% traffic. health: OK. metrics snapshot: errors 0.12%, p95 420ms.

amy: Plan: 30m canary -> 30% -> 100% if green. If we hit the safety gate we'll follow the runbook sequence (unpin, route traffic back to v2.3.x, and run postmortem). If unpin expected >1h impact, escalate to exec comms.

mike: Standing by. Ping me if you need rollback DB sanity checks or logs.

jordan: Thanks — I'll post a short checklist when I start the unpin so Support can follow along. (react: :thumbsup:)
__notes: single-thread Slack export style; messages concatenated in order with display names prefix. No title per agents.md.
